newsitem.title: ISRAEL: End of the line for Israeli bus to Cairo.
newsitem.headline: End of the line for Israeli bus to Cairo.

text.p: Israel's public transport company said on Thursday it was ending its bus service to Egypt for lack of interest 18 years after the two states made peace.
The Egged corporation was losing 3,000 shekels ($900) every time a bus made the 12-hour trip from Tel Aviv to Cairo with only about 10 riders, said spokesman Ron Ratner.

"The main factor is economic. In the last two years we've seen a steady decline in passengers on a line that's expensive to run. There is simply less interest today (among Israelis) in Egypt," he told Reuters.
The last bus to Cairo will leave Tel Aviv on Sunday and return to Israel on Monday, Ratner said, leaving Israelis with the alternatives of flying or taking a chartered bus to Egypt.
The line was inaugurated in 1982, three years after Israel signed a peace treaty with Egypt, its first with an Arab state.

Peace after four wars with Egypt sparked euphoria in Israel but relations between the two countries have at times been tense, most recently over Jewish settlement construction in the occupied West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Hundreds of Israelis travelled on the line every week during the 1980s but Egged cut its service in recent years to just once a week due to the drop in demand.

A Palestinian attack on an Israeli tourist bus in Egypt in 1990 killed nine Israelis and led to a sharp drop in Israeli tourism. Ratner said the government turned down Egged's request to subsidise the line.
